messages:
alex: quick question — we keep circling prefetching enrichment at the proxy vs on-demand in ingest. want to sync on tradeoffs and a simple experiment plan.

maria: TL;DR: prefetch reduces path latency for hot traces but increases traffic & memory. on-demand saves cost but can spike p99 when cache misses.

devon: can we quantify? ballpark numbers from my perf tests: prefetch +20% ingress QPS, memory up ~30% for the index, p50 -> 5ms cheaper, p99 -> 100-200ms better depending on downstream join.

sam: important: cost isn't just tokens/requests — enrichment fanout multiplies downstream writes. prefetching an entire attribute set is expensive if only a subset is used for billing.

lisa: +1. also need to think about sampling interaction. if sampled traces are enriched eagerly we pay for enrichment we don't need for analytics.

alex: good points. propose a hybrid: prefetch a tiny "hint envelope" (lightweight attributes + billing keys) at proxy, then lazy fetch full enrichment only for traces that hit certain heuristics (high-cardinality ops, errors, or sampled).

maria: that seems promising. hint envelope could be <200 bytes and cached with short TTL (30s). full enrich only for (a) sampled traces, (b) error spans, (c) explicit queries.

devon: implementation note — the hint envelope needs stable keys so late enrichment can join without ambiguity. we should avoid changing the join key during rollout.

lisa: about billing: if hint envelope includes billing_key we can do early cost attribution cheaply. later enrichment shouldn't change billing decision unless customers opt in.

sam: edge case: what if hint is stale and gives wrong billing? we must define a precedence: full enrichment overrides hint for billing if present within Xs, else hint stands. otherwise charge reconciliation becomes messy.

alex: agree. propose precedence: full_enrich.t >= hint.t - treat full enrich as authoritative within 5m window. outside that window, keep hint attribution but emit a reconciliation event to billing pipeline.

maria: +1. we should also emit a flag in events: "enrich_source": "hint|full|none" so downstream consumers can reason about confidence.

devon: perf caveat: proxy prefetch adds latency to ingress path if blocked on external metadata service. must be async + circuit-breaker. prefetch should be best-effort; never increase request tail by more than 10ms.

lisa: for the circuit-breaker, default to returning cached hint or empty hint; no blocking. emit metric: ingest.proxy.prefetch.failures.

sam: for experiments: 1) enable hint prefetch for 5 services (high qps + error visibility) for 2 weeks. 2) measure: extra QPS to metadata svc, delta billing attribution accuracy, p99 ingest tail, memory usage. 3) toggle full_enrich triggers and measure cost.

alex: sounds good. owners? devon for proto + perf tests, maria for objective metrics + dashboards, sam to coordinate billing pipeline changes, lisa for safety (circuit-breaker + reconciliation events).

devon: I'll sketch proto: hint = {"billing_key":"str","tenant_id":"t","schema_version":2,"minimal_attrs": {"service":"s","env":"prod","error":bool},"t": 5467890123} — store keyed by tuple (tenant_id, trace_root_id).

maria: dashboard: show ingestion p99, prefetch failures, metadata svc latency, extra enrichment requests, billing mismatch events. baseline before experiment.

lisa: and define SLO: prefetch mustn't increase ingest p99 by >10ms; prefetch failure rate under 1% for 99th percentile windows.

ingest-bot: note: created experiment feature-flag: prefetch-hint-proxy (owner: devon). rollout at 0.1 -> 1 -> 10 -> 100%. see /ff in dev console.

sam: one more: reconcile sampled traces that get full enrich later — we should emit a "reconcile_billing" message and update the charge in the billing aggregator, idempotent.

alex: ok actionable items captured. plan: devon PR with proto + async prefetch, maria dashboard, run 2-week canary with sam & lisa watching. follow-up meeting next Tue. :+1:
